a router doesn't protect your anonymity at all, nor is that its purpose. A router is really just used to allow multiple devices to share a single internet connection. In the case of personal routers at home, this allows all your devices to connect to a single uplink (your cable/dsl modem) via a router. Without a router, you'd need separate connections to your cable/dsl modem for each device that you intend to use with its connection. That being said, some routers DO have privacy features built in. One that I like personally is from anonabox.com - they have several offerings, but their pro offering (which is like $75 if I remember correctly) allows you route all connections through both a VPN and/or TOR (www.torproject.org if you aren't familiar with what this is, some people call TOR "the dark web"). You don't really need to be using a VPN at the router level though - most people are satisfied using it for a particular device only, so that not every single device of yours connects to the internet through that VPN (it can slow things down). I'll explain below why/how it's usually sufficient to install a VPN on your device rather than through your router.

The 2 (router and VPN) are usually considered entirely separate though. When you use a VPN service, your traffic is encrypted, even though it is technically still going through your home connection's router. The reason for that is that VPNs utilize end to end encryption (which is effectively the same reason your ISP can't spy on your credit card info everytime you order something from Amazon - because it's using end-to-end SSL encryption). Basically this means that your data is encrypted/decrypted at only 2 points - YOUR device and the VPN you're connecting to. Your ISP would be able to see the metadata associated with these connections, so they'd be able to tell you were using a VPN, but the actual content would be unreadable to them (since it'd be encrypted). There's a pretty good extension for Chrome-based browsers called Free-VPN.pro that you may want to check out. There are a ton of such extensions available (do a search and see), but the reason I like this one is because it's free, fast, and allows you to easily/quickly change VPNs based on the country where you'd like to connect to the VPN service (many people do this to get around content restrictions, like certain tv/movies only being available to stream in certain countries). Obviously if you choose a country that's far away geographically, it's probably going to slow your connection down as you go further and further. Most people would tell you that TOR provides better anonymity/privacy than a VPN. Imo, they're too different to compare, but this article might help you to understand the differences: https://www.privateinternetaccess.com/pages/tor-vpn-proxy - personally I find TOR slow, so I don't use it all the time, but for those who really want an extra degree of anonymity and don't mind compromising their speed for it, TOR is probably the best option.
